main_text.p: ¶. 109. Sixtin. de regalib. lib. 1. cap. 4. n. 118. D. Brandmuller. d. Prælim. dissert. cap. 6. pag. 11. Frantzkius ad §. 9. instit. de jur. nat. gent. & Civil. quam auctoritate constituentis, Sam. Marefi. in Diss. de jur. Canon. §. 20. & 21. idque propter Processum judiciarium, qui in libro secundo Decretalium & passim in sequentibus collectionibus, ex interpretibus Juris Civilis, & propriis figmentis, rerum emergentium varietate materiam & modum suggerente, magis concinne est explicatus: item alias quasdam materias, Jurisjura idi[?], Matrimonii & similes; Vid. Reinkingius de regin. secul. & Eccles. lib. 2. classe 2. c. 7. Quæ tamen aliunde hauriri possent, nisi usus invaluisset; qui solus etiam sustinet titulum Doctoris Juris Canonici, qui simul datur cum Doctoratu Juris Civilis, ne opus sit propter conversationis frequentiam cum Pontificiis, pati ab iis status controversiam; qua de re potest videri Casp. Zieglerus, §. 68. dict. dissertat. & Sam. Marefi. de Jure Canon. §. 19. ante Cucchi institut. Ubi varias adferunt rationes, quare professio & titulus Doctoris in Jure Canonico hodie ad hoc sustineatur in territoriis Protestantium; Quibus adde quæ supra prolixè disputavimus de auctoritate Gratianei Decreti: ex qua disputatione satis conclu-

page.notes: The first line opens with a reference fragment ("¶. 109.") continued from the previous page; the "¶" may be a printed mark. "Jurisjura idi" appears to be a broken word (Jurisjurandi); the gap is doubtful. The catchword "di po-" stands at the lower right and is not part of the text. Some italic and roman words, and the reference "n." in the first line, are set in mixed type; the italic on "nat.gent." and "classe" is read as printed.
